title: Chapter 140: The Different Levels of Scary Scenarios
html:
Wang Wenlong sat at the bottom of the old well, punching wildly at the air as though fighting an invisible boxing match.

“Stay here. I’ll pull him out,” Chen Ge told Pei Hu. At the sound of his voice, Wang Wenlong stopped. He slowly raised his head, dazed and traumatized. Then his lifeless gaze found Pei Hu and sharpened.

Anger shook Wang Wenlong’s body and broke whatever grip terror held on him. “You f*cker! You dare show your face again?”

“Listen to me. It was a dangerous situation. If I didn’t run, we both would have been in danger.”

“You lie!”

“It’s true. I used myself as bait and lured away the worst threat. Ask the boss if you don’t believe me.”

Pei Hu felt deeply wronged. No one who had not spent ten minutes trapped under a bed in a staring contest with a severed head could understand.

“Keep your voices down. Continue the argument outside.” Relieved by Wang Wenlong’s vigor, Chen Ge reached down. “Give me your hand.”

Wang Wenlong stopped shouting when he saw Chen Ge. “I can’t. My lower body is numb.”

“Numb?” Chen Ge jumped down, and with Pei Hu’s help, hauled Wang Wenlong out. He did not leave immediately. When hiding the tags that morning, he had inspected the well and found nothing frightening beyond the two mannequins.

Aboveground, Wang Wenlong and Pei Hu resumed arguing. Chen Ge crouched beside the buried figures. Unlike that morning, the male mannequin’s eyes were open.

These mannequins represent Fan Yu’s parents. If they were Baleful Specters, they would be far harder to control. Thankfully, they are only lingering spirits.Chen Ge remembered what had happened to Fei Youliang. When the Pen Spirit possessed him and tried to escape, the spirits from the sealed classroom stopped her.

They had entered Fei Youliang’s body and marched him to the well, apparently intending to punish the Pen Spirit before stopping at the last moment.

The Pen Spirit was at fault. Did the others bring her here because they intended to imprison her in the well?

Looking at Fan Yu’s parents buried in the sand confirmed his suspicion: the old well served as a prison for malicious lingering spirits.

Come to think of it, the spirits in the sealed classroom possess a strong sense of justice.

In life, every one of them had been an orphan adopted by the old headmaster. Mu Yang High School became their home. Now that the black phone had rebuilt it inside the Haunted House, the spirits probably wanted only a stable, peaceful existence.

As long as you behave, my Haunted House can be your new home.

Chen Ge looked once more at the buried mannequins and climbed out. When he glanced back, both pairs of eyes had closed.

“Come on. It’s time to leave.” Chen Ge helped Wang Wenlong stand. Fear still filled the man’s eyes; only anger at Pei Hu had briefly overwhelmed it.

After tremendous effort, Chen Ge finally shepherded all five visitors out. When the entrance curtain opened, the waiting crowd gasped. They had heard the nonstop screams but never imagined the group would emerge in such a state.

“What have these people experienced?”

“It was only half an hour…”

Uncle Xu, diligently selling tickets, noticed everyone staring past him. Dread gathered in his stomach. When he turned, his hair stood on end.

“Damn! What happened?” Uncle Xu abandoned the booth and rushed to support Wang Hailong and Xia Meili.

“Only a small fright. Nothing serious.” Chen Ge released Wang Wenlong’s arm. “Can you walk?”

When they heard Chen Ge, the visitors all took a step back.

“He could not even walk, and you say that’s a little scare?!”

“Are you trying to lie to us?!”

Embarrassed by the crowd, Wang Wenlong tottered forward like a toddler taking his first steps.

“Wenlong! Pei Hu!” A muscular man in a tank top pushed through the crowd, a wolf’s head tattooed on his shoulder. He caught Wang Wenlong. “What happened? We heard you screaming outside.”

This was the sixth member of their group—the man who, according to plan, should now attempt the challenge alone.

“Were we that loud?” Wishing the ground would swallow him, Wang Wenlong brushed away the man’s hands. When he refused to explain, the newcomer confronted Chen Ge. “What did you do to my brother?”

“Brother?” The man’s tone struck Chen Ge as odd, but he dismissed it and faced the crowd. “Before they entered, I warned everyone that the scenarios have different levels. Visitors should complete the easier ones before attempting a higher fear rating. They ignored me and insisted. You can see the result.”

Ignoring the muscular man, Chen Ge adopted a serious expression. “When I proposed tiered scenarios, many accused me of chasing money. That isn’t true. I want to protect my customers. The new Two-Star Scenario is not suitable for everyone; its fear rating exceeds anything offered by other Haunted Houses.”

Gripping the gate, Chen Ge continued. “Western Jiujiang’s Haunted House has operated for years, and our rating has never fallen below ninety percent because we put customers first. If you accept the challenge, we will give you the most frightening experience of your life.

“But everyone’s tolerance is different. We pursue the ultimate scare, yet some scenarios may overwhelm first-time visitors. After careful consideration, we therefore divided our attractions into levels.”

The visitors had to accept the new system. The prize money tempted them toward the harder scenario, while Wang Hailong’s group demonstrated the consequences of ignoring its prerequisites.

“If you want the prize, follow the rules. Complete the lower-level scenarios before challenging the harder ones.”

The system would keep every scenario relevant. More importantly, each newly unlocked attraction with a higher Scream Factor would draw thrill seekers back, laying the foundation for his future horror theme park.
